surprises.description: PFG’s reported Q3 EPS was $2.22, below the preview’s $2.30–$2.42 base range, because the after-tax drag from lower-than-expected variable investment income and Encaje was 27 cents—larger than the 10–20 cents the preview expected to isolate. Excluding significant variances, EPS was about $2.49, within the preview’s expected $2.42–$2.52 range, so the shortfall was concentrated in the variance bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 non-GAAP operating earnings were $482 million ($2.22 EPS), but lower-than-expected variable investment income and Encaje performance created a $59 million ($0.27 per share) after-tax drag.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the base case was “Reported EPS $2.30–2.42” and expected encaje and alternatives to be “isolated at 10–20c”; it gave an ex-variance range of “$2.42–2.52.”

surprises.description: Total-company net cash flow was close to flat at negative $11 million, much better than the preview’s concern about continued pressure after Q2’s $11.1 billion outflow and its bear case of investment-management outflows worse than $5 billion. U.S. retail active equity strategies still had outflows, but the overall flow result was far less negative than the preview’s risk framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total company net cash flow was negative $11 million in the quarter,” with outflows in U.S. retail active equity strategies; management expected near-term pressure to persist.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted Q2 enterprise AUM net cash flow of “−$11.1B,” asked whether the “$10B committed-but-not-funded pipeline” funded, and described a bear case of “IM outflows worse than −$5B.”

surprises.description: Private markets and active ETFs brought in $1.3 billion of positive net cash flow combined, and active ETF AUM reached $14 billion, up 84% year over year. The preview focused on whether the investment-management pipeline funded but did not anticipate these specific inflows or the ETF growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Private markets generated $800 million and active ETFs $500 million of positive net cash flow in Q3, with active ETF AUM reaching $14 billion, up 84% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: PFG said full-year buybacks are now expected toward the low end of the target range because of the unplanned Beam acquisition, rather than simply reaffirming the capital-deployment plan the preview expected. Q3 buybacks themselves were $250 million, matching the amount highlighted in the preview’s Q2 baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year buybacks now expected toward the low end of the target range due to the unplanned Beam acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said capital deployment had a “$1.5–1.8B FY target,” was “back-half weighted,” and its base scenario expected FY deployment to be “reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Life insurance adjusted pretax operating earnings rose 29% and its margin expanded 420 basis points, a much stronger operating result than the preview’s only life-specific estimate—fees up 2.2%—would suggest. The preview did not provide an earnings or margin forecast for the segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Life insurance adjusted pretax operating earnings jumped 29% to $39 million with margin up 420 basis points to 16.4%, driven by improved mortality frequency and severity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Life Insurance — fees: $115.3M | +2.2%” and did not give a segment earnings or margin expectation.

surprises.description: International pension AUM was $166 billion, above the preview’s $164.3 billion estimate, and earnings grew 11%. The AUM beat was modest; the preview did not forecast pension earnings growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International pension earnings grew 11% with AUM up 10% to $166 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “International Pension AUM” at “$164.3B.”

surprises.description: Despite a 59% overall Specialty Benefits loss ratio, individual disability had elevated claims volatility, an adverse detail not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of favorable incidence and a loss ratio expected below guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Specialty Benefits had “a 59% loss ratio,” though “individual disability saw elevated claims volatility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management expected the loss ratio below the 60–64% range because of “dental network optimization and favorable incidence,” and described a 58–60% result as validating the margin story.
